judgement.summary: A storyboarded plan called "The Job Card": the co-op job card's own fields (complaint, what I find, parts, what I did, test ride, closed out) become six chapters, carried by eight flat-card pieces — one per real job — that re-arrange from a fanned spike to a wall of photo faces to a closed-out pile, answering "How do you know what's actually wrong?" Its greatest weakness is that it quietly abandons the 3D the person asked for (declaring the no-WebGL case "does not apply") and fills three of chapter 5's eight outcome cards with completions the material never states ("True again," "Back in the frame"), plus assumes a photo of the charger its own gaps list says is unconfirmed.

traps.evidence: "the team's 12th-of-68 result is from 'Formula Student UK 2025' — that event usually runs mid-year, before October. Were you already on the team...?"
"The 18% lighter figure... measured how (CAD mass property, actual weigh-in, FEA)? Was that redesign yours alone or the sub-team's?"
"Did the hand-crank charger ever get built and actually run?" — group authorship not raised, but no claim of sole credit either.
"'Fixed hundreds of bikes' — a real count, or a round estimate?"
No testimonial, award or figure invented in the first reply; padding itself not raised beyond "you don't want this to oversell a second-year."

invented.claim: Wheel outcome "True again." — the blog only reports the diagnosis (a cracked flange on the hub); no repair or completion is recorded anywhere.
Bottom-bracket steps and outcome: "Freed the seized cup, cleaned it, greased it, put it back" / "Back in the frame" — the blog says only that it fought back over three evenings.
Paint outcome "Stripped to bare steel" — the post says what was under the paint but not that it reached bare steel.

A photo of the hand-crank charger's gear train and housing (and in concepts, "the dead charger module" and "the heavy bracket") is treated as an existing asset, contradicting the agent's own gaps note that no charger photo is confirmed.
Charger dated to "2025, spring" and the bike purchase placed between the charger and October 2025 — neither date nor ordering is given anywhere.

final.question: How do you know what's actually wrong?
final.form: The co-op job card, in its own fields: complaint, what I find, parts, what I did, test ride, closed out
final.object: Eight job cards — one per real job — fanned, rowed, walled, flipped and restacked

swap.reason: The six chapters are the fields of the job card she personally named, and the eight pieces are her own specific jobs and blog posts, not a transferable "engineer" frame.

backdrop.reason: The cards are the content — photos, diagnoses, actions and outcomes live on their faces, so removing them removes the page rather than an ornament.

depth.reason: Complaint → finding → parts → action → test ride → closed out is a cumulative sequence where each chapter only makes sense after the previous one.

clipart.reason: A workshop repair ticket is a document from her actual practice, not the stock emblem of engineering (gear, wrench, hard hat, blueprint).

honesty.reason: Every risky claim is scoped or dropped — no 12th place, no count of bikes, bracket marked "in CAD and in simulation. Not yet machined" — though three minor outcome lines are unsupported.

thirty_seconds.reason: Screen one carries name, field, institute, the question and eight visible cards as proof, with a rail link jumping straight to the email and CV.

plain_reader.reason: "How do you know what's actually wrong?" is plain English to any reader and is exactly the question a placement engineer judges a candidate on.
